title: Waves run wider than one: no file every task must edit
description: Owner 2026-11-25, answering how to speed development up: today almost every task declares CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, so the drive's wave builder sees a shared file between any two tasks and runs waves of width one (register F915). Make those two files stop being a per-task collision, then measure the wave width it buys. FIRST TASK (materialize with /audit:task add on this phase; key changelog-fragments, risk med, tdd): A task writes its changelog entry as a fragment of its own, and the release assembles CHANGELOG.md from the fragments. Every task appends to CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section, so every pair of tasks shares that file and the wave builder runs them one at a time (F915). Replace the shared append with one fragment file per task (the towncrier pattern: changelog.d/<task-id>.<kind>.md, kind one of the section words the changelog already uses), assembled into CHANGELOG.md by the release step (tools/release.py) and checked by a lint that the assembled text equals what the release would write. Decide and state: where the fragments live, what a fragment that names no kind does, how the existing [Unreleased] text is carried (move it into fragments once, so nothing is lost), what tools/release.py, verify.sh --release and CONTRIBUTING.md's release step now do, and how `/audit:task add` and the executor brief tell a task to write a fragment instead of editing CHANGELOG.md. The same question for PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: list which of its per-module sections can be generated from the code the way the module map already is (tools/lints/_deps.py --render), and either generate them in this task or file a follow-up with the list; a hand-written section a task must still edit stays a declared file. Acceptance: two tasks that touch different modules and each write a fragment are planned as one wave by the drive (show it with the wave builder on a fixture plan); release output on this repository is byte for byte the current CHANGELOG.md plus the assembled fragments; the doc lints stay green; measure the wave width the next phase actually gets and record it. Files: tools/release.py, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, tools/verify.sh, tests/test_release.py. tests.add: tests/test_release.py: the release assembles CHANGELOG.md from the per-task fragments and an assembled text that differs from what the release would write is refused
desiredOutcome: Two ready tasks of one phase that touch different code run as one wave: no task declares CHANGELOG.md or a hand-written section of PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md only to describe itself, and the release still produces the same CHANGELOG.md.

findings.issue: step_commit deletes the fragments from disk (os.remove) BEFORE `git rm`. If `git rm` fails (reproduced on a real scratch git repo with a held .git/index.lock) the step returns False, but the files are already gone from disk while still tracked in HEAD. A resumed step_commit then sees no fragments (read_fragments reads disk), so fragment_findings/assembled_findings return [] and consumed is empty: it commits successfully, and the release commit still carries changelog.d/P9.1.added.md in HEAD (git ls-files changelog.d lists it). The next release assembles that already-released fragment a second time. unconsumed_findings also reads disk only, so verify --release cannot see it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P170.2-yl6 (88ee8a78f0df): Make the deletion one git operation that leaves state intact on failure: run `git rm -q -f --ignore-unmatch -- <fragments>` first (it removes the working file too) and only then os.remove any untracked leftover; or on resume derive `consumed` from `git ls-files changelog.d` as well as the directory. Add a case with a runner whose git rm returns non-zero asserting the files are still on disk and a second step_commit still removes them.

findings.issue: The task says 'If deriving every section is too large for one small task, derive the mechanism and one representative section, and file the rest as a follow-up task in P170 with the list.' The diff derives layer, kind, suite and importers, and names the undone parts only in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md section 1b ('Not derived: a module's public names ... and an entry's usage line'). P170 holds three tasks (P170.1, P170.2-yl6, P170.3-yl6) and none is a follow-up for public names, the entry usage line, or the tree section's file list. The remainder is therefore not tracked anywhere a gate or the ready list reads.
findings.resolution: File the follow-up in P170 (/audit:task add) listing what the filed return measured: public names (needs a per-module block, one line cannot hold them), entry usage line (needs a USAGE constant per entry), and the tree section's file list.

tasks.title: A task writes its changelog entry as a fragment of its own, and the release assembles CHANGELOG.md from the fragments
tasks.description: First task of P170 (read the phase description in docs/audit/phases/P170.json; it is the authority). Every task appends to CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section, so every pair of tasks shares that file and the wave builder runs waves of width one (register F915). Replace the shared append with one fragment file per task (towncrier pattern: changelog.d/<task-id>.<kind>.md, kind one of the section words the changelog already uses), assembled into CHANGELOG.md by the release step (tools/release.py finalize-changelog) and checked by a lint that refuses a fragment with an unknown kind and an assembled text differing from what the release would write. Decide and state in CONTRIBUTING.md: where fragments live, what a fragment naming no kind does, that the existing Unreleased text stays as written and the fragments are appended under it at release (nothing moved, nothing lost), what tools/release.py and verify.sh --release now do. This repository's own instruction to tasks (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) says write a fragment, not CHANGELOG.md. The plugin's product (executor brief, /audit:task add) is NOT changed here: name what it would take as a follow-up. Acceptance: release finalize on a fixture yields byte for byte the Unreleased text plus the assembled fragments in a stated order; an unknown kind and a hand-edited assembled section are refused, each red-first; doc lints green; show with the drive's wave builder on a fixture plan that two tasks touching different modules and each writing a fragment are one wave, where the same two declaring CHANGELOG.md are two.

outcome.technical: tools/release.py: added changelog fragments (changelog.d/<task-id>.<kind>.md; KINDS = breaking, added, changed, deprecated, removed, fixed, security, documentation, compatibility, each a heading word CHANGELOG.md already uses - rl31 reads the file). read_fragments/fragment_findings refuse a name with no kind, an unknown kind, an empty file and a body with its own ##/### heading, never skip them. assemble_fragments writes ### <Kind> per kind in KINDS order, task ids in numeric order (P170.2 before P170.10). release_text renames ## [Unreleased] and appends the assembled text after the existing section text, which is not edited (no fragment -> only the heading changes, rl27c). step_finalize_changelog refuses on findings, and on resume refuses a section that no longer ends with the assembled text; step_commit re-checks, deletes the consumed fragments and stages them with git rm --ignore-unmatch. New command release.py changelog-check [--repo] [--version]: without a version the fragment lint, with one also the assembled-section check and fragments left beside the section. tools/verify.sh: lint slice row 'changelog fragments are ones the release can place' (changelog-check), release slice row after changelog_has_section (changelog-check --version). tools/gate-parity.py needs no edit and stays green. CONTRIBUTING.md Release rule states where fragments live, what a kind-less fragment does (refused), that the Unreleased text stays as written with fragments appended under it, the order, and what release.py/verify.sh now do. CLAUDE.md Releasing: a task writes a fragment, never CHANGELOG.md. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: its release sentence names the assembled section. Wave proof (rl33, plus _wave.select run directly): two tasks on different modules each declaring its own fragment -> {wave: [P1.1, P1.2], deferred: []}; the same two declaring CHANGELOG.md -> {wave: [P1.1], deferred: [{id: P1.2, reason: overlap, with: P1.1}]}. Coverage rule: tools/ files carry their own selftest cases via tools/_suite.run, so the cases are in tools/release.py (_fragment_cases, reached through _cases_all); no tests/test_release.py was created. changelog.d/P170.1.changed.md is this task's own entry (scope since widened by the orchestrator). CHANGELOG.md is untouched. Dependants (guard-release.py, check-example-pins.py, tests/test__refs.py, sweep-costs.json, ci.yml): all still correct. Follow-up the product needs, not done here: the executor brief (agents/audit-executor.md and the brief builder's text) and /audit:task add still tell a task to edit CHANGELOG.md; they need to name changelog.d/<task-id>.<kind>.md. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md generate-sections question is not in this task. git rm in step_commit was only exercised against FakeRunner, not a real git index.
outcome.descriptive: Tasks now write their changelog entry as a fragment under changelog.d/ and the release assembles CHANGELOG.md from them, so two tasks on different modules no longer collide on CHANGELOG.md and the wave builder runs them as one wave.

tasks.description:
step_commit deletes the fragments from disk (os.remove) BEFORE `git rm`. If `git rm` fails (reproduced on a real scratch git repo with a held .git/index.lock) the step returns False, but the files are already gone from disk while still tracked in HEAD. A resumed step_commit then sees no fragments (read_fragments reads disk), so fragment_findings/assembled_findings return [] and consumed is empty: it commits successfully, and the release commit still carries changelog.d/P9.1.added.md in HEAD (git ls-files changelog.d lists it). Resolution asked: Make the deletion one git operation that leaves state intact on failure: run `git rm -q -f --ignore-unmatch -- <fragments>` first (it removes the working file too) and only then os.remove any untracked leftover; or on resume derive `consumed` from `git ls-files changelog.d` as well as the directory. Add a case with a runner whose git rm returns non-zero asserting the files are still on disk and a second step_commit still removes them.

outcome.technical: tools/release.py step_commit: removed the os.remove-before-git-rm; it now runs `git rm -q -f --ignore-unmatch -- <fragments>` first (git removes the working file with the index entry, and a refusal removes neither), returns False on failure leaving files on disk and tracked, and only after success os.removes any fragment git did not track (isfile-guarded). New case rl30c in _fragment_cases on a real scratch git repo (tempfile.mkdtemp via _fragment_fixture, remove_tree in finally, held .git/index.lock): the first step_commit fails and fragments remain on disk and in git ls-files; after releasing the lock a resumed step_commit succeeds and both disk and ls-files are empty (add/commit are stubbed, git rm is real). Dependants: tests/test_audit_task.py, guard-release.py, check-example-pins.py, ci.yml, sweep-costs.json etc. use release.py via import/path of other functions (release_verdict, _read_text, save_state); step_commit's signature and return shape are unchanged, so still correct. CONTRIBUTING.md names `finalize-changelog`, untouched. No file outside tools/release.py edited; no fragment owed by the brief.

tasks.description: Second half of P170's description: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md is the other file nearly every task declares (a section headed by a module's path is a reader of that module, so the start refusal asks for it), which also caps the drive's waves at one. Measure first: over the last two landed phases (P169, P170) count how many tasks declared PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and which part of each guide section they edited. Then list the guide's per-module sections and, for each, which part is derivable from code the way the module map fence already is (tools/lints/_deps.py --write-map / render): layer, imports, importers, public names, the entry's usage line. Derive the parts that can be derived in a fenced, generated block per section (or one generated index) checked by test__deps the way g1 checks the module map, so a code change no longer obliges a hand edit of the guide; the hand-written rationale stays and stays declared when a task changes what it says. If deriving every section is too large for one small task, derive the mechanism and one representative section, and file the rest as a follow-up task in P170 with the list. Record the measured counts in the return. Changelog line: changelog.d/P170.3.changed.md (the fragment convention P170.1 introduced; CONTRIBUTING.md).
